findings.title: Equal-order crypto providers are now chosen silently
findings.body: detectProvider used to fail fast when ServiceLoader found more than one CryptoProvider. It now sorts by order() and keeps the first, only logging the rest. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so a classpath that contains both FIPS and non-FIPS (or Elytron and default) no longer errors. ServiceLoader order is classpath order, and sorted() is stable, so which full provider wins is environment-dependent. ServiceLoader also instantiates every provider before the sort, so FIPS1402Provider still inserts BCFIPS/BCJSSE and rewrites key/trust manager security properties even if the non-FIPS provider is the one selected (and DefaultCryptoProvider still registers BouncyCastle). A FIPS deployment can therefore keep running in a mixed or non-FIPS mode instead of refusing to start. Tie at the winning order should still be a hard error, and FIPS must outrank the non-FIPS providers if silent preference is intended.

findings.title: New abstract order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: order() was added as an abstract interface method with no default. CryptoProvider is a public SPI in keycloak-common. Existing downstream or custom implementations (and any already-compiled class) will not have this method. ServiceLoader instantiates every provider and then calls order() during sort, so one old implementation on the classpath throws AbstractMethodError and aborts detection entirely, even if a newer provider is also present. That turns a compatible server startup into a hard failure. A default method (for example returning 0) would keep old providers loadable and still let the new order-200 providers win.

findings.title: AuthzClient.create can permanently install the stub crypto provider
findings.body: AuthzClient.create now calls CryptoIntegration.init with AuthzClient's own classloader, and init only selects a provider when the static cryptoProvider field is still null. That selection is process-wide and never refreshed. AuthzClientCryptoProvider is registered via META-INF/services and implements almost every CryptoProvider method by throwing UnsupportedOperationException, with order 100. If create() runs before the server calls init with a classloader that can see DefaultCryptoProvider or FIPS1402Provider (deployment/module classloader that only exposes the authz-client service file, embedded startup, or a test that builds an AuthzClient first), the stub is locked in for the JVM. Later server init is a no-op, so token signing, PEM handling, and the other crypto entry points fail or use the incomplete provider even though a real one is on the server classpath.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK keystore provider
findings.body: The CryptoProvider contract says getBouncyCastleProvider returns the non-FIPS or FIPS BouncyCastle provider. This implementation returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is the platform provider for the default keystore type (typically SUN), not BC or BCFIPS. Callers use that Provider's name and instance for Cipher/Signature/CertificateFactory and for BouncyIntegration. Algorithms that exist only under BC (AES/CBC/PKCS7Padding, many JOSE/JWE transforms, BCFKS) will fail or silently run outside FIPS when this provider is the one CryptoIntegration selected. Elytron returns null rather than a lookalike; this should not hand back an unrelated JCA provider.

findings.title: ECDSA test does not compile in this module
findings.body: ECDSAAlgorithmTest imports org.keycloak.crypto.ECDSAAlgorithm and org.keycloak.crypto.JavaAlgorithm. Those types live in the server SPI (the crypto modules already import them from there), not in keycloak-core. authz/client/pom.xml only adds junit and hamcrest; its compile/test classpath is still just keycloak-core plus HTTP/Jackson. server-spi is not a dependency, and keycloak-core cannot depend on server-spi without a cycle. testCompile of keycloak-authz-client-tests therefore fails with a missing org.keycloak.crypto package, so the new coverage never runs.

findings.title: ECDSA transcoding test never checks a real signature
findings.body: The only assertion is that asn1derToConcatenatedRS and concatenatedRSToASN1DER round-trip each other. The key pair is generated once with KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC"), which is P-256 on standard JDKs, and that same key is used for ES256, ES384, and ES512. ES384/ES512 signature lengths are 96 and 132 bytes and their DER SEQUENCEs need long-form lengths once R and S match P-384/P-521, but a P-256 signature stays short and is only zero-padded to those lengths. Nothing calls Signature.verify on the original DER or on the re-encoded DER, and there is no known-answer vector. A self-consistent but non-interoperable encoder (wrong tag, non-minimal INTEGER, broken long-form length) still passes, which is the failure mode this provider exists to prevent.
